key_insight: Two supervised psilocybin doses over two weeks were feasible and were associated with meaningful short-term reductions in OCD symptoms in a small open-label trial.
clinical_relevance: This suggests psilocybin may be a potential adjunct for treatment-resistant OCD, but it remains investigational and not established as standard care.
method: 30 analyzed participants with prior failed psychotherapy or pharmacotherapy; 37 were enrolled total.
Waitlist-controlled open-label randomized design at Johns Hopkins.
Two doses: 20 mg psilocybin, then 30 mg if tolerated, with supportive monitoring.
evidence_signal: Compared with waitlist, the immediate-treatment group had significantly lower Y-BOCS scores after dosing (F(2,56)=16.17, p<0.001), with effects persisting after crossover.
watch_item: Small sample size, open-label design, and limited follow-up mean the results may overestimate benefit and need confirmation in larger blinded trials.
paper_title: An Open-Label Multidose Psilocybin Intervention for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
